chunks: Muhammad ibn Hammam narrated to us; he said: Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Issam narrated to me; he said: Abu Sa'id Sahl ibn Ziyad al-Adami narrated to us; he said: Abdul Adheem ibn Abdullah al-Hasani narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Rida (peace be upon him), that he heard him say:

When my son Ali dies, a lamp will appear after him and then it will disappear. Woe to the doubter, and blessed is the stranger who flees with his religion. After that, there will be events that make the young hair turn grey and the deaf, hard-hearted ones will move.

key_terms.النَّوَاصِي: The forelocks/hair of the head (symbolizing youth)
key_terms.الْفَارِّ بِدِينِهِ: The one who flees/preserves his religion
key_terms.سِرَاجٌ: Lamp (symbolizing spiritual guidance or the Imam)

ai.seo_question: What are the signs following the death of Imam Ali ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) specifically identifies the son as Ali ibn Muhammad (the 9th Imam, often called Ali al-Naqi), linking the 'hiding of the light' to the Minor Occultation (al-Ghaybah al-Sughra) and the subsequent rise of the Major Occultation. The 'turmoil' described reflects the historical context of political instability and the testing of the faithful during the transition of authority, emphasizing that true success lies in those who remain steadfast despite the 'hair turning white' from prolonged waiting. This hadith serves as a foundational text in Shia eschatology for understanding the nature of the Imam's disappearance as a divine trial rather than a mere absence.
